fields-block.comment: A field name, type and modifier are all free identifiers, so an activation is unreadable from one field line alone; the block boundary is what tells the two apart.

field-name.comment: A field line's first token, whatever it spells. Claiming it here is what keeps the flat alternation and #keyword-entity off a field named after a keyword: both match further along the line, and the leftmost match wins. A name position admits every spelling, so there is no per-spelling axis to key on and the rule is positional, like #positional-keywords, rather than an allowlist. It reaches only a name opening its own line — the block's opening line is already consumed by begin, which is why fields { command string required } is left as it was.

patterns.comment: Keywords followed by quoted entity name
Keywords followed by identifier entity name
target keyword with type and trailing entity name

positional-keywords.comment: Keywords that read as keywords only in one position — an automation's two activation forms, the delay qualifying either, and an event's wire type — so each is keyed on its operand rather than joining the flat alternation, which would paint a field named after one. Deliberately case-sensitive, unlike the rules above: the lexer's keyword lookup is too, so On, Every, After and Type are legal entity names.

patterns.comment: Event-driven activation and the event it names
Schedule-driven activation; the schedule itself stays a string literal
patterns.name: keyword.control.emod

patterns.comment: The delay qualifying an activation; the duration itself stays a string literal
patterns.name: keyword.control.emod

patterns.comment: An event's wire type; the value itself stays a string literal
patterns.name: keyword.control.emod

keywords.comment: Every lexer keyword except on, every, after and type, which #positional-keywords colours case-sensitively so a field named after one stays a field. Longer spellings precede the shorter ones they contain (events before event, tags before tag) to keep the alternation readable; the surrounding \b makes the order immaterial.
keywords.name: keyword.control.emod

payload-values.comment: A payload's numeric and boolean values, keyed on the colon introducing them the way #positional-keywords keys its entries on their operand. Positionless would paint a field named true, and every digit the language writes outside a payload — a version header's among them, which the tree-sitter query leaves uncaptured too. #strings precedes this in #standalone-tokens, so neither pattern reaches inside a quoted value carrying digits. Case-sensitive, like the grammar's own boolean token.
